claims.text: Rep. Cynthia McKinney (D-Ga.), a five-term incumbent, lost her August 2002 primary to former judge Denise Majette 58% to 42%; Majette had strong support from out-of-state pro-Israel contributors (no figure given), Republicans crossed over to vote in the Democratic primary, and McKinney blamed Republican voters.
Rep. Earl Hilliard (D-Ala.), also critical of Israel, lost a primary runoff about two months before McKinney; Black Caucus leaders questioned the role of pro-Israel money in his defeat.

claims.text: In 2022 UDP spent about $4.26M against Donna Edwards and $1.7M for Glenn Ivey (MD-4, Ivey won); $3.88M for Haley Stevens and $342,000 against Andy Levin (MI-11, Stevens won); $2.74M for Adam Hollier and $1.43M against Shri Thanedar (MI-13, Hollier lost); $2.13M for Valerie Foushee (NC-4, won); $2.1M for Don Davis and $335,000 against Erica Smith (NC-1, Davis won); $2M against Summer Lee and $660,000 for Steve Irwin (PA-12, Lee won); $423,000 for Henry Cuellar and $1.43M against Jessica Cisneros (TX-28, Cuellar won).

In 2024 UDP raised about $68.4M through August and spent about $56M; it spent almost $9.9M opposing Jamaal Bowman and nearly $4.8M supporting George Latimer (NY-16; Latimer won 25 June with over 58%); more than $5.2M against Cori Bush and $3.3M for Wesley Bell (MO-1; Bell won 6 Aug); about $4.6M against Dave Min (CA-47; Min advanced); about $3M against four Republican House candidates, two of whom (John Hostettler, IN; Rep. Bob Good, VA) lost; about $12.4M supporting some Democrats and more than $20M opposing others; top donors Jan Koum $5M, Jonathon Jacobson ~$4.6M, Bernard Marcus $3M, David Zalik $2M.

The New York Times said UDP's NY-16 spending 'eclipsed what any interest group has ever spent on a single House race'; after Latimer's win AIPAC said UDP 'will continue to support leaders who promote our partnership with Israel'.

AdImpact counted $30.7M in ad spending by UDP, the RJC Victory Fund and DMFI PAC in 2024 House primaries by 5 July 2024, including UDP $14.9M in NY-16 (59% of the race's spending), $3.6M in MO-1, $4M in CA-47, $3.7M for Sarah Elfreth in MD-3, $1.8M against John Hostettler (IN-8) and $1.2M against Brandon Herrera (TX-23), with the RJC Victory Fund $1.2M for Mark Messmer (IN-8).

The Guardian found the top six 2022 recipients of pro-Israel donor spending, all centrist Democrats who beat progressives, received about $25M (about 42% of the total), including nearly $5.4M backing Haley Stevens and about $2.8M backing Don Davis; DMFI claimed its candidates won over 80% of 2022 races.

claims.text: In the NJ-11 special Democratic primary (Feb 2026) UDP spent more than $2.3M in independent expenditures against Tom Malinowski, with ads saying he 'voted with Trump and the Republicans to fund ICE'; Analilia Mejia, who has said Israel committed genocide in Gaza, won by 889 votes in an 11-candidate field; AIPAC's spokesperson said 'Our six million members will be very active this election cycle'; FactCheck.org puts UDP's spending against Malinowski at over $2M.

In the 17 March 2026 Illinois primaries AIPAC-linked spending exceeded $21M across four Chicago-area House races, routed largely through new committees (Affordable Chicago Now, Elect Chicago Women) and in IL-7 through UDP directly (about $5M for Melissa Conyears-Ervin, who lost); its candidates won two of four (Donna Miller IL-2, Melissa Bean IL-8) and lost two (Conyears-Ervin IL-7, Laura Fine IL-9, where Daniel Biss won); about $92M was spent on the four House races and the Senate race combined.

UDP spent more than $30.6M in the 4 August 2026 Michigan Democratic Senate primary supporting Haley Stevens and opposing Abdul El-Sayed, AIPAC's largest spending on a single race; El-Sayed won; AIPAC said its members 'remain determined to ensure that voters reject Dr. El-Sayed and his radical anti-Israel agenda in November'.

In the CA-14 special election runoff of 18 August 2026 Aisha Wahab beat Melissa Hernandez 53% to 47% after UDP spent $2.4M to boost Hernandez and gave over $1.5M to BOLD America, which spent over $2M helping her.
UDP spent over $1M supporting Adrian Boafo, who won the MD-5 primary of 23 June 2026; FactCheck.org counted UDP aligned with its goal in four of five listed 2026 races.

American Priorities, a super PAC formed on 12 February 2026 to counter AIPAC, pledged over $10M, raised $3.85M in January–March 2026, spent about $1M for Nida Allam (NC-4, lost by under 1%), about $2M for Adam Hamawy (NJ-12, won), over $400,000 for Chris Rabb (PA-3, won) and $2M for three New York candidates on 23 June, two of whom defeated AIPAC-endorsed incumbents Dan Goldman and Adriano Espaillat (per Wikipedia).

claims.text: Rep. Thomas Massie (R-KY) lost the 19 May 2026 primary to Trump-endorsed Ed Gallrein, 54.9% to 45.1%, in the most expensive House primary on record (about $37M in all; $32.6M in ads, per AdImpact).

Pro-Israel PACs spent about $8M against Massie: UDP $4.1M and the RJC Victory Fund $3.9M (Louisville Public Media); FactCheck.org counted UDP spending over $3M against him and nearly $500,000 for Gallrein; Politico counted over $9M from pro-Israel groups; a Trump-aligned super PAC, MAGA KY, spent about $7.4M.

Trump recruited and endorsed Gallrein (endorsement of 17 October 2025), and AP judged Trump the key factor; Massie had crossed Trump on the Epstein files, the Iran strikes and the 2025 tax-and-spending law.

AIPAC congratulated Gallrein for 'defeating anti-Israel incumbent Thomas Massie'; UDP's spokesperson called Massie 'the most anti-Israel Republican in the House'; Massie said a 'foreign lobby has fully funded' the effort 'to the extent that they've never done in any Republican race ever before'.
